newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU 14 refinery output up 0.1 percent - Euroil.
newsitem.headline: EU 14 refinery output up 0.1 percent - Euroil.

text.p: Net refinery output in the 14 nations of the European Union, excluding Sweden, was slightly higher in September, despite falling fuel oil production, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.

Refinery output in September rose 17,000 barrels per day (0.1 percent) to 11.791 million bpd, while refinery crude intake was up 39,000 bpd (0.4 percent) to 11.179 million bpd. This represented a utilisation rate of 88.72 percent, against 88.41 percent in August.
Year-on-year, output was up 48,000 bpd (0.4 percent).

Italy's production increased by most in September, up 130,000 bpd (7.6 percent) to 1.837 million bpd, while output in the Netherlands was down the most, falling 165,000 bpd (10.2 percent) to 1.460 million bpd.
The modest overall increase in output came despite a large decrease in fuel oil production, down 64,000 bpd (3.8 percent) to 1.622 bpd.
Middle distillate output was only up 4,000 bpd (0.1 percent) to 5.273 from August, but was 139,000 bpd (2.7 percent) higher than in September 1995.
Gasoline production fell 20,000 bpd (0.6 percent) in September to 3.195 million bpd. This was 111,000 bpd (3.4 percent) lower than in September 1995.
Naphtha output was up 43,000 bpd (5.0 percent) to 895,000 bpd.
They are based on a nameplate capacity of 12.6 million bpd. Refinery intake represents crude only and excludes natural gas liquids, feedstocks and other inputs.
